clue.text: Kremlin's first to intervene in news agency assignments

indicators.note: to intervene in something is to come between its parts, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: TASS was the official Soviet news agency

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Kremlin's

explanation.surface: Moscow's leader steps in to manage what the state news service is told to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to intervene in' puts K, the first letter of Kremlin, inside TASS, the Soviet-era Russian news agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs given to someone, which is exactly what assignments are.

clue.text: See 4 across
Adriatic port targets problem with locks

parts.note: Split is a port city on the Adriatic coast of Croatia
ends are aims or goals, as targets are

explanation.surface: A Croatian harbour town sets its sights on some troublesome locking mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are frayed tips of hair, a common complaint about one's locks (tresses).

clue.text: Furore when hill is captured by sergeantmajor

indicators.note: being captured by something means being held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SM is the standard abbreviation for sergeant major
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Uproar breaks out when a senior NCO seizes the high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is captured by' is the container signal; SM for sergeant major is a common military abbreviation, and a tor is a craggy hill typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean an outburst of anger or controversy, a synonym of furore.

clue.text: Milton's moving words — the awesome, wondrous words of transport arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the preceding letters means they are put in a new order

parts.words: the awesome, wondrous words of transport

explanation.surface: A tribute to a poet's stirring line, couched in the language of a travel timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals the anagram of all 34 letters of THE AWESOME WONDROUS WORDS OF TRANSPORT. 'transport arrangement' masquerades as travel plans. The answer is the famous last line of Milton's poem Lycidas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the closing line of Lycidas, about moving on to new places, so it is literally words of Milton about moving.

clue.text: That's funny, Barry goes off, having alternated

parts.note: Barry Took was a British comedy writer and broadcaster, so a funny Barry is Took
milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the oddity of a man called Barry wandering away after switching back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Took was a British comedy writer (co-creator of Marty Feldman's shows and host of The News Quiz), hence 'That's funny, Barry'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to do something alternately, one after another, so having alternated is having taken turns.

clue.text: Fit for encounter

definitions.meaning: an old word for suitable or proper

explanation.definitionFit: Meet as an adjective means fitting or proper, and as a verb means to encounter someone.

clue.text: Property accounts for having broken bread?

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn or broken
rolls are small loaves of bread

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether ledgers of property earn their name by having torn up some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the cryptic reading pulls the compound apart: torn bread is rent rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent roll is a register of a landlord's properties and the rents due on them, an account of property.

clue.text: Start playing notes

indicators.note: playing notes about suggests jumbling them into a different order

explanation.surface: A musician begins by sounding a few notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram of NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, as of an illness or of winter, so it means a start.

clue.text: Sees no alternative after second innings but to take the obvious course

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come behind the cricket term

parts.note: in cricket the follow-on is a team's second innings, forced on it straight after its first

indicators.note: an alternative version of the words Sees no is a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A cricket team forced to bat again has no choice but to carry on in the plainest way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' makes ESNOSE from SEES NO, and 'after' puts it behind FOLLOW ON, a cricket term for a side made to bat its second innings immediately because it trailed badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow one's nose is an idiom meaning to go straight ahead or act on instinct, taking the obvious course.

clue.text: Totally fair conditions?

parts.note: the proverb says all is fair in two situations, romance and combat, so those are the conditions where anything goes

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'all's fair in love and war' names two circumstances in which everything is considered fair.

clue.text: Value of property? About one million

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the property word goes round the other letters

parts.note: an estate is a piece of landed property
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking what a house is worth, and getting a guess of about a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts ESTATE around I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge the worth of something, which is to value it.

clue.text: Conch blower cut short musical interval

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a tritone is a musical interval of three whole tones

explanation.surface: Someone sounding a shell horn stops abruptly mid-note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final E of TRITONE, the interval of three whole tones.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Triton, son of Poseidon, blows a conch shell to calm or raise the waves.

clue.text: Jack joined men on board twice

parts.note: hands are the sailors aboard a ship
a crew is the body of sailors aboard a ship, the second synonym asked for

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack signs on with the ship's company not once but twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for two different synonyms of 'men on board': HANDS and CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A handscrew is a type of lifting jack worked by turning a screw by hand.

clue.text: Bird seed with smoother exterior

indicators.note: an exterior is an outside layer, so the smoother word wraps round the seed

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
a pip is a small fruit seed

explanation.surface: A bird food is improved by giving it a smoother outer coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' is the container signal; 'with' is only a link. 'Bird seed' looks like a single phrase about feeding birds, but 'Bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a wading shorebird with a long bill.

clue.text: Drink ready for American antelope

parts.note: water is something to drink, and the drink is a name for the sea
ready means cash, and an American word for a dollar is a buck

explanation.surface: Someone prepared for a drink with an American beside a herd animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash (ready money); 'for American' asks for the US word BUCK, a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterbuck is a large African antelope that lives near water.

clue.text: Key may be associated with this slow movement

definitions.text: Key may be associated with this
definitions.meaning: An island in the Florida Keys and a famous Bogart film
a movement played very slowly and broadly is so marked in music

explanation.definitionFit: Largo pairs with Key in the Florida island name, and is also an Italian tempo marking for a slow, broad piece of music.

clue.text: Borderline Wayne western

definitions.meaning: the river forming much of the border between the USA and Mexico
a 1950 cowboy film starring John Wayne, directed by John Ford

explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande river forms a national border, and Rio Grande is a John Wayne cavalry western.

clue.text: Valentine's brother or child of Welles

parts.note: a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is a sibling of Valentine or the offspring of the film director Welles.
explanation.walkthrough: In the medieval romance Valentine and Orson the two heroes are twin brothers; 'of Welles' nods to the actor Orson Welles.
explanation.definitionFit: The French romance Valentine and Orson tells of twin brothers separated at birth, one raised by a bear.

clue.text: These oars could be transferred from boat

indicators.note: letters transferred are moved into new positions, giving a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Oars may be shifted out of a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be transferred' signals the anagram of THESE OARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something ashore is to unload it from a boat on to land.

clue.text: Public prosecutor and Mafia boss return to the beginning

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
a capo is the head of a Mafia crime family

explanation.surface: A prosecutor and a mob leader go back to where it all started.
explanation.definitionFit: Da capo is an Italian musical instruction to repeat from the start of the piece.

clue.text: Walkover for military leader's horse

parts.note: C-in-C stands for commander-in-chief, the head of the armed forces
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A general's steed wins without a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, which gives H as in drugs slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is something very easy, as is a walkover, an easy win.

clue.text: Number of copies produced of picture for all to see in the navy

parts.note: a print is a picture made from a plate or photograph

indicators.note: in says the piece goes inside the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
U is the British film certificate for a universal audience, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Copies of a picture are printed for everyone in the fleet to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside RN; U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A print run is the number of copies of a book or paper printed at one time.

clue.text: Born on the outskirts of Paris with Scottish roots

parts.note: née, used before a maiden name, means born

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so take the first and last letters of Paris

explanation.surface: Someone born at the edge of the French capital has ancestry in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives P and S, the first and last letters of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps is the Scots word for turnips (swedes), root vegetables eaten with haggis.

clue.text: Capital raised in Bolsover

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the letters come in reverse
in says the letters lie inside the word Bolsover

explanation.surface: Money is raised in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside BOLSOVER to OLSO, and 'raised' turns it round. Bolsover is a town in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: See 4
Tea with jam and mustard — that's wild

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
a lock or jam is a situation where things are stuck fast, as in a wrestling hold

explanation.surface: A picnic offering tea with jam and mustard, which is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wild' looks like an exclamation of disgust, but it says the mustard is the wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a yellow-flowered weed of fields.

clue.text: Downright female monarch

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen who is utterly straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means utter or complete, as downright does in 'sheer nonsense'.
